title: Combined IAC Vulnerabilities: Public S3 Bucket Misconfigurations (Terraform and Pulumi) and Privileged Kubernetes Pod with In-Container Secrets
description:
This combined IAC vulnerability captures three separate misconfigurations observed across the codebase:
1) Terraform: Publicly accessible S3 bucket with public-read-write ACL, no server-side encryption, and no versioning demonstrated in main.tf (aws_s3_bucket.public_data). Absence of encryption and versioning, plus a permissive ACL, enables data leakage, tampering, or loss. A bucket policy is not shown to restrict access, and the bucket could be used for hosting or exfiltrating data and serving as a foothold for further compromise.
2) Pulumi: Another S3 bucket with public-read-write ACL and force_destroy, with explicit comments indicating no encryption or versioning. Publicly writable storage compounds risk of data exposure, manipulation, or persistence of malicious content. Force_destroy further increases usability of destructive actions (deleting non-empty buckets) without additional safeguards.
3) Kubernetes Deployment: A pod running a container as root in privileged mode with ALL capabilities, plus sensitive credentials embedded in environment variables and plaintext ConfigMap-based secrets. The image nginx:latest is used (no pinning), and there are no resource limits, probes, or service account restrictions, creating opportunities for privilege escalation, container break-out, credential exposure, and lack of runtime defense. All three issues collectively create a broad attack surface: improper cloud resource exposure, weak container isolation, and insecure secret handling.
suggested_fix: For Terraform S3 bucket: remove public-read-write ACL; set to private or use a restrictive bucket policy granting access only to specific IAM principals; enable server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS); enable versioning; implement Block Public Access at the account/bucket level; review and restrict website hosting configurations; remove or tighten force_destroy usage. For Pulumi S3 bucket: set ACL to private or implement a strict policy restricting access; disable force_destroy or limit to controlled deletion; enable encryption at rest (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS) and versioning; enable access logs and Block Public Access. For Kubernetes deployment: avoid running containers as root or in privileged mode; drop all unnecessary capabilities; run as a non-root user with readOnlyRootFilesystem; pin image versions (avoid latest); remove hardcoded secrets from environment variables (use Kubernetes Secrets or external secret management); apply resource requests/limits; add liveness/readiness probes; restrict access via a non-privileged service account and consider Pod Security Policies or Gatekeeper rules to enforce least privilege.
snippet:
Terraform snippet:
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "public_data" {
  bucket = "my-public-data-bucket-12345"
  acl    = "public-read-write"  # VULNERABILITY: Public access
}

Pulumi snippet:
bucket = aws.s3.Bucket(
  "public-data-bucket",
  acl="public-read-write",
  force_destroy=True,
  # VULNERABILITY: No encryption, no versioning
)

Kubernetes snippet:
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 0
        runAsNonRoot: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest  # VULNERABILITY: Using latest tag
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
          runAsUser: 0
          capabilities:
            add:
            - ALL
        env:
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          value: "password123"  # VULNERABILITY: Hardcoded password
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "sk-1234567890abcdef"  # VULNERABILITY: API key in plain text
        - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
          value: "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE"
        - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
          value: "wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY"
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "my-jwt-secret-key"  # VULNERABILITY: Secret in env var
"},{

title: RDS instance publicly accessible with unencrypted storage and weak credentials
description: Pulumi script defines an AWS RDS MySQL instance with storage_encrypted=False and publicly_accessible=True, exposing the database to the internet without encryption at rest. The admin password is a weak value (password123). skip_final_snapshot=True reduces protection by skipping an automated final snapshot. This combination creates a high risk of data exposure, tampering, and persistent compromise if credentials are leaked.
suggested_fix: Enable storage_encrypted with a KMS key (storage_encrypted=True, kms_key_id set); disable public accessibility (publicly_accessible=False) or restrict access via security groups/VPC; store credentials securely (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) and enable IAM database authentication if possible; deploy in private subnets with proper network controls; enable automated backups; rotate credentials and do not rely on skip_final_snapshot in production; ensure proper backup and recovery strategies.
snippet:
database = aws.rds.Instance(
  "database",
  engine="mysql",
  engine_version="5.7",
  instance_class="db.t2.micro",
  allocated_storage=20,
  storage_encrypted=False,  # VULNERABILITY: No encryption
  publicly_accessible=True,  # VULNERABILITY: Public access
  db_name="mydb",
  username="admin",
  password="password123",  # VULNERABILITY: Weak password
  skip_final_snapshot=True,
)
